gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Anker SOLIX PS200 panel in the C1000 Gen 2 kit has a 57.6 V open-circuit voltage against the station's 60 V solar limit, so the 600 W input can't be filled by wiring PS200s in series (two would reach 115.2 V). A second panel has to go in parallel. The station's input also splits into two bands: 11–28 V capped at 8.2 A, and 29–60 V at up to 14.5 A.
standout_why: I compared against the cited rival pages Lights On Labs, StormWatts (same panel watts), SolutionEnergy and PowerSized. StormWatts gives the C1000 Gen 2 only as '600 W, 60 V max'. It covers series and parallel wiring for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 and the Jackery SolarSaga 500 X, and DC8020 limits for the Explorer 2000 v2, but gives no PS200 voltage. SolutionEnergy has part of the finding: 'up to 600 W at 29–60 V' and 'Anker PS200 48 V output'. It leaves out the 11–28 V / 8.2 A low band, the PS200's 57.6 V Voc and the series ban. PowerSized covers the BLUETTI AC180's DC7909 input versus the MC4-to-XT60 cable, but nothing on Anker. Lights On Labs gives only generic advice.
decides: This confirms that the C1000 Gen 2 + PS200 kit is a sound value pick out of the box: the 48 V panel runs in the 29–60 V band, so the 8.2 A low-band cap doesn't hold it back. It also qualifies the '600 W, 1.8 h' upgrade path. PS200s added later must be wired in parallel, not in series, and the C1000 Gen 2 can't take an expansion battery. A shopper planning to add solar should budget for a parallel lead or pick a 12–24 V-class panel pair wired in series. A single 12 V-class panel would charge in the 8.2 A band. It doesn't overturn the pick, but it's the one Anker detail the rival pages are missing.

findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station (Anker SOLIX US store)
findings.note: Quoted from the spec section: '11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)'. Anker's UK kit page gives the same figures and names the port as 'XT60i Input Port'. In the low band, power is capped at 8.2 A × panel voltage, so at most 229.6 W even at 28 V. Reaching 600 W needs the high band (600 W ÷ 14.5 A ≈ 41.4 V minimum).

findings.note: Arithmetic: 2 × 57.6 V = 115.2 V, which exceeds the 60 V max on https://www.ankersolix.com/products/c1000-gen2. A single PS200 at 48 V Vmp runs in the 29–60 V / 14.5 A band, so it isn't held back by the 8.2 A low band. Adding panels toward 600 W means parallel wiring into the one XT60i input. None of the Anker pages I opened names a parallel lead.
